Generating Stimuli for the Allergist Task

Source: vignettes/stimuli-allergist-task.Rmd
stimuli-allergist-task.Rmd

This copy was built without access to the OSF images, so the stimulus code is shown but not run. Set-up section below says how to run it.

In this vignette, we use catlasr::catlas_stimulus() to generate and save stimuli, both cues and outcomes, for the Allergy task used for replication and extension studies of Beesley and Le Pelley (2011).

The stimuli consist of:

  • cues comprising a name of a fictional chemical below a flask icon, and
  • outcomes comprising a cartoon of potential side effect above its label
library(catlasr)
library(tibble)
library(gt)

Set-up

Currently, images for stimulus generation are hosted on OSF. To access them from R, you will need a Personal Access Token (PAT) for the osfr package.

  1. Ensure you are listed as a contributor on the private CATLAS project.
  2. Create a PAT in your OSF account settings.
  3. Open your .Renviron file via usethis, add the token as OSF_PAT=<your token>, and restart R:
usethis::edit_r_environ()

Before creating the stimuli, download materials from OSF to a temporary directory:

temp_path <- file.path(tempdir(), "my_osfr_downloads")
dir.create(temp_path)

osfr::osf_retrieve_node("2shuc") |>
  osfr::osf_ls_files(n_max = 15) |>
  dplyr::filter(name == "stimuli") |>
  osfr::osf_download(temp_path, recurse = TRUE, conflicts = "rewrite")

Cues

Since Beesley and Le Pelley (2011) do not provide the full list of fictional chemicals used in their study, naming only Addexium and Rezaline as examples, the current study uses chemical names from Le Pelley et al. (2007). Not only did the latter study use the same experimental design, but the authors also provided all 28 cue labels employed by them.

Additionally, the two example chemical names from Beesley and Le Pelley (2011) and four new fictitious chemical names generated using Google’s Gemini (https://gemini.google.com) were added to be presented in experiment tutorial.

Cue Stimulus Generation

To generate a cue stimulus, we need the flask image, and the stimulus label. The flasks image for current study was generated by Gemini Nano Banana 2 model to resemble images used in Scenario 2 of Le Pelley et al. (2010).

The image is then:

  • combined with appropriate label to yield cue stimulus via catlasr::render_stimulus()
  • saved to the target location where experiment code lives via catlasr::write_stimulus() 
flask_path <- file.path(
  temp_path,
  "stimuli",
  "templates",
  "allergy_task",
  "flasks.png"
)

#label <- "Ulginát" # Czech version
label <- "Ulginate" # English version

stim <-
  catlasr::catlas_stimulus(
    label = label,
    image_path = flask_path,
    type = "cue"
  )
  
img <-
  catlasr::render_stimulus(
    stim,
    width = 200, height = 200,
    font_size = 32,
    label_position = "bottom",
    label_shift = c(0, 20),
    background = "#c1c1c1"
  )

plot(img)
# Demonstration only, do not run
if (FALSE) {
  catlasr::write_stimulus(
    img,
    here::here(
      "forward-blocking-experiment",
      "stimuli",
      "cues",
      "Ulginate.png"
    )
  )
}

Language Conversion

Since the original article was conducted in English, while parts of the replication and extension take place in Czech, the chemical names were converted using a set of rules documented in below.

English Czech Rule
Le Pelley et al. (2007)
Ulginate Ulginát Functional Group Mapping: The English chemical suffix "-ate" is replaced by the Czech equivalent "-át", reflecting the standardized naming of salts and esters in Czech nomenclature.
Renphane Renfan Consonant Orthography & Functional Group Mapping: Latin/English consonant cluster "ph" is adapted to Czech phonetic spelling "f", and the suffix "-ane" is mapped to the Czech equivalent "-an" used in alkane nomenclature.
Nelomine Nelomin Suffix Truncation: Silent trailing vowel "-e" is removed to conform to Czech morphological patterns and pronunciation conventions.
Kluphane Klufan Consonant Orthography & Functional Group Mapping: Latin/English consonant cluster "ph" is adapted to Czech phonetic spelling "f", and the suffix "-ane" is mapped to the Czech equivalent "-an" used in alkane nomenclature.
Bizancrine Bizankrin Consonant Orthography & Functional Group Mapping: The letter "c" is replaced to preserve a hard "k" sound in Czech spelling, and the suffix "-ine" is mapped to the Czech equivalent "-in" used in amines and alkaloids.
Alzaze Alzas Suffix Truncation: Silent trailing vowel "-e" is removed to conform to Czech morphological patterns and pronunciation conventions.
Quezalin Kvezalin Consonant Orthography: Foreign letter combination "qu" is adapted to Czech phonetic spelling "kv" to preserve pronunciation while matching Czech orthographic conventions.
Xentine Xentin Suffix Truncation: Silent trailing vowel "-e" is removed to conform to Czech morphological patterns and pronunciation conventions.
Frestix Frestix No Adaptation Required: The name already conforms sufficiently to Czech orthographic and phonological conventions.
Trizopane Trizopan Suffix Truncation: Silent trailing vowel "-e" is removed to conform to Czech morphological patterns and pronunciation conventions.
Lobinz Lobinz No Adaptation Required: The name already conforms sufficiently to Czech orthographic and phonological conventions.
Zapotyne Zapotyn Suffix Truncation: Silent trailing vowel "-e" is removed to conform to Czech morphological patterns and pronunciation conventions.
Fazakane Fazakan Suffix Truncation: Silent trailing vowel "-e" is removed to conform to Czech morphological patterns and pronunciation conventions.
Jintsone Jintson Suffix Truncation: Silent trailing vowel "-e" is removed to conform to Czech morphological patterns and pronunciation conventions.
Eframide Eframid Suffix Truncation: Silent trailing vowel "-e" is removed to conform to Czech morphological patterns and pronunciation conventions.
Sistax Sistax No Adaptation Required: The name already conforms sufficiently to Czech orthographic and phonological conventions.
Kikaran Kikaran No Adaptation Required: The name already conforms sufficiently to Czech orthographic and phonological conventions.
Ontone Onton Suffix Truncation: Silent trailing vowel "-e" is removed to conform to Czech morphological patterns and pronunciation conventions.
Pukintz Pukintz No Adaptation Required: The name already conforms sufficiently to Czech orthographic and phonological conventions.
Gratix Gratix No Adaptation Required: The name already conforms sufficiently to Czech orthographic and phonological conventions.
Ventox Ventox No Adaptation Required: The name already conforms sufficiently to Czech orthographic and phonological conventions.
Cucose Cukóza Functional Group Mapping: The English carbohydrate suffix "-ose" is replaced by the Czech equivalent "-óza", following the established Czech naming convention for sugars.
Yestimox Yestimox No Adaptation Required: The name already conforms sufficiently to Czech orthographic and phonological conventions.
Halorite Halorit Suffix Truncation: Silent trailing vowel "-e" is removed to conform to Czech morphological patterns and pronunciation conventions.
Prental Prental No Adaptation Required: The name already conforms sufficiently to Czech orthographic and phonological conventions.
Goladine Goladin Suffix Truncation: Silent trailing vowel "-e" is removed to conform to Czech morphological patterns and pronunciation conventions.
Ilomine Ilomin Suffix Truncation: Silent trailing vowel "-e" is removed to conform to Czech morphological patterns and pronunciation conventions.
Daktyre Daktyr Suffix Truncation: Silent trailing vowel "-e" is removed to conform to Czech morphological patterns and pronunciation conventions.
Beesley & Le Pelley (2011)
Addexium Adexium Orthographic Simplification: Double consonants are reduced because Czech generally does not preserve consonant doubling in loanword adaptation unless it carries a phonological distinction.
Rezaline Rezalin Suffix Truncation: Silent trailing vowel "-e" is removed to conform to Czech morphological patterns and pronunciation conventions.
Gemini
Vextrine Vextrin Suffix Truncation: Silent trailing vowel "-e" is removed to conform to Czech morphological patterns and pronunciation conventions.
Quanzane Kvanzan Consonant Orthography & Functional Group Mapping: Foreign letter combination "qu" is adapted to Czech phonetic spelling "kv", and the suffix "-ane" is mapped to the Czech equivalent "-an" used in alkane nomenclature.
Meltrizene Meltrizen Suffix Truncation: Silent trailing vowel "-e" is removed to conform to Czech morphological patterns and pronunciation conventions.
Sintrizide Sintrizid Suffix Truncation: Silent trailing vowel "-e" is removed to conform to Czech morphological patterns and pronunciation conventions.

Outcomes

Following Beesley and Le Pelley (2011), four outcomes were used for the current study: dizziness, headache, itchiness, and nausea. Two further outcomes, coughing and rash, were used in the tutorials.

Each outcome option consisted of a black-and-white cartoon depiction of a man suffering given symptom accompanied by symptom label below the picture.

For experimental trials, two fictitious patients, Mr. X and Mr. Y, were generated, each suffering each of the four symptoms. For tutorial trials, one fictitious patients, Mr. Z, was generated suffering the two additional symptoms.

Outcome Stimulus Generation

Outcome stimuli are generated in much the same way as the cue stimuli, using appropriate cartoon images available in the OSF repository (downloaded earlier in this vignette).1 Each image is combined with its label via catlasr::render_stimulus() and saved via catlasr::write_stimulus().

image_path <- file.path(
  temp_path,
  "stimuli",
  "templates",
  "allergy_task",
  "z_coughing.png"
)

#label <- "kašel" # Czech version
label <- "coughing" # English version

stim <-
  catlasr::catlas_stimulus(
    label = label,
    image_path = image_path,
    type = "outcome"
  )
  
img <-
  catlasr::render_stimulus(
    stim,
    width = 400, height = 436,
    font_size = 66,
    label_position = "bottom",
    label_shift = c(0, 20),
    background = "#ffffff"
  )

plot(img)
# Demonstration only, do not run
if (FALSE) {
  catlasr::write_stimulus(
    img,
    here::here(
      "forward-blocking-experiment",
      "stimuli",
      "outcomes",
      "z_coughing.png"
    )
  )
}

Outcomes List

English Czech Patient
dizziness závrať X and Y
headache bolehlav X and Y
itchiness svědění X and Y
nausea nevolnost X and Y
coughing kašel Z
rash vyrážka Z

Conclusions

  • This vignette demonstrates the generation of all stimuli required for the Allergist task replication and extension of Beesley and Le Pelley (2011).
  • Cue stimuli (34 in total) were drawn from Le Pelley et al. (2007) (28 names), Beesley and Le Pelley (2011) (2 names), and Gemini (4 tutorial names).
    • Nine conversion rules were applied to adapt English chemical names to Czech orthographic and phonological conventions, with all mappings documented in the rule book above.
  • Outcome stimuli comprise six symptom images (four experimental, two tutorial), each rendered for fictitious patients in both languages.

References

Beesley, T., and M. E. Le Pelley. 2011. “The Influence of Blocking on Overt Attention and Associability in Human Learning.” Journal of Experimental Psychology: Animal Behavior Processes 37 (1): 114–20. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0019526.
Le Pelley, M. E., T. Beesley, and M. B. Suret. 2007. “Blocking of Human Causal Learning Involves Learned Changes in Stimulus Processing.” Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology 60 (11): 1468–76. https://doi.org/10.1080/17470210701515645.
Le Pelley, M. E., Mia Schmidt-Hansen, Naomi Jane Harris, Catherine Maria Lunter, and Charlotte Sonia Morris. 2010. “Disentangling the Attentional Deficit in Schizophrenia: Pointers from Schizotypy.” Psychiatry Research 176 (2-3): 143–49. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.psychres.2009.03.027.
